outcome: maternal intestinal microbiome composition and diversity
cohort: A cohort of 167 mothers (with a subset of 100 mothers for microbiome and cortisol determination) from whom data were collected during the first four months post-partum.
finding: The mode of delivery and co-dominant hormonal changes, particularly salivary cortisol concentration, significantly influence maternal microbiota composition and diversity, and impact maternal weight recovery during the post-partum period.
mod_finding: Maternal microbiota was significantly influenced by the mode of delivery, with the vaginal delivery group exhibiting significantly higher salivary cortisol concentration and lower post-partum weight retention than C-section mothers at four months post-partum.
